The **Imjin War** (also known as the **Japanese invasions of Korea** or the **Japanese–Korean War**) was a series of conflicts that took place from 1592 to 1598 between the Japanese forces of Toyotomi Hideyoshi and the Korean Joseon dynasty, with assistance from Ming China. Here’s a concise overview: | Aspect | Details | |--------|---------| | **Timeframe** | 1592–1598 | | **Key Players** | • **Japan** – led by Toyotomi Hideyoshi.
• **Korea (Joseon)** – led by King Seonjo.
• **Ming China** – intervened to support Joseon. | | **Causes** | • Hideyoshi’s ambition to conquer China via Korea.
• Desire to expand Japanese influence and secure trade routes. | | **Major Phases** | 1. **First Invasion (1592–1593)** – Japanese forces captured Seoul and much of the peninsula.
2. **Ming Intervention** – Chinese troops joined Korean forces, pushing back Japanese armies.
3. **Second Invasion (1597–1598)** – Japanese attempted to regain lost territory but were ultimately defeated. | | **Key Battles** | • Battle of Hansan Island (1592) – naval victory for Korea.
• Battle of Noryang (1598) – decisive naval engagement that ended the war. | | **Outcome** | • Japan withdrew after Hideyoshi’s death and internal strife.
• Korea suffered massive destruction and loss of life.
• Ming China’s resources were heavily strained. | | **Legacy** | • Strengthened Korean naval technology (e.g., turtle ships).
